page: Amazon Web Services mac-m4max.metal is a dedicated bare-metal instance designed for macOS workloads, categorized under the General Purpose family. The server is powered by an Apple arm64_mac processor featuring 16 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. Because it is a bare-metal deployment without virtualization hypervisors, all CPU resources are dedicated with a single thread per core.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per CPU core. The instance provides no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for file persistence and operating system storage. Discrete hardware accelerators are absent, with a reported GPU count of zero. Network connectivity is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In terms of operational efficiency and hardware tradeoffs, the dedicated hardware profile delivers consistent clock execution and substantial memory capacity per core. However, the lack of local NVMe storage places all disk I/O demands onto network-attached storage architectures, making overall throughput reliant on the 10 Gbps network interface.

This hardware profile is tailored specifically for Apple ecosystem development, continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, macOS application compiling, and automated testing tasks requiring native arm64 execution and substantial memory buffers.
